PS-A3 (`New-Object` as a CONSTRUCTOR CALL). Authored 2026-09-27, from hand-auditing the F5 differential's MISSING samples. Three spellings of the same cmdlet, and only one was read: `-TypeName <managed type>`. `-ComObject <ProgID>` was not read AT ALL, so `New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application` published no edge rather than a wrong one, and the POSITIONAL form `New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList` published none either. The F5 samples show `instantiates Extract-ZipLegacy -> Shell.Application` on ansible's own Windows modules, so the shape is common in the corpora rather than hypothetical.

The fixture also pins the guard that keeps this honest in the other direction: `-TypeName string` is a type ACCELERATOR and constructs nothing the graph should name, and a bare `New-Object` with no argument has nothing to construct. Both are `forbid` rows, so the fix cannot be widened into silence.

And it pins a mistake this work made and caught before committing: the first version keyed `isComObject` on the constructed name containing a dot, so `-TypeName System.Text.StringBuilder` was published as a COM object. The FLAG decides the kind, never the spelling of the type — a dotted .NET name and a COM ProgID look alike and mean different things. The two metadata rows below are what caught it.

expectRelationships.comment: The COM form. `-ComObject` is not a rarer spelling of `-TypeName`, it is the ONLY spelling for a COM object, and `$shell = New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application` is how the language gets a Shell handle. The ProgID is dotted and external by nature, which is the designed handling for a name the file does not declare.

The flagged .NET form. `meta.isComObject: null` is the load-bearing part and it is an ASSERTION, not a note: the runner's `meta.x: null` convention means "this edge must NOT carry x", which is the only channel that can say a label is absent. Keying the flag on the constructed name containing a dot published this row as a COM object, and the first version of the fix did exactly that — a comment could not have caught it, and the `com-object-keyed-on-a-dot` mutant survived until this row said it.

The POSITIONAL form, written whenever the author did not bother with a flag. `commandArgs` returns values only, having skipped every `command_parameter`, so the first entry is the type name and the flagged forms leave it empty.

forbidRelationships.comment: PRE-FIX-CLASS, kept deliberately: `New-Object -TypeName string` constructs a type ACCELERATOR, which is a PowerShell language primitive rather than a declared type, and naming it would put `instantiates -> string` in the graph. The `isTypeAccelerator` guard exists so this cannot happen, and this row is what stops the guard being widened away while fixing the positional form.
A bare `New-Object` has no argument and nothing to construct; an edge here would name an object the source never mentions.

PS25 — the WORKING half of the `meta.isComObject: null` assertion above, and the row that actually kills `powershell/com-object-keyed-on-a-dot`. The two rows say the same thing in the runner's two vocabularies, and only this one is enforced: `matchConstraints` in `script/m14/run-fixtures.ts` reaches its top-level `if (v === null)` branch (line 338) BEFORE its `k.startsWith("meta.")` branch (line 358) and `continue`s, so `meta.isComObject` is looked up as a TOP-LEVEL key that never exists on a relationship. Measured, both directions, through the exported `matchConstraints`: an edge that DOES carry `isComObject: true` still satisfies `{ "meta.isComObject": null }` -> true, and an edge that does not carry it -> true. The assertion is therefore TRUE for every analyzer, correct or defective, and the null-metadata convention is a no-op for 16 expectation rows across 6 lanes (yaml 4, vue 1, typescript 1, svelte 1, powershell 1, bash 1). The array-valued `meta.*` case directly above it was fixed for exactly this routing bug (the comment at line 320 records it, and two elixir mutants had survived); the `v === null` case has the identical shape and did not get the same fix. `script/m14/run-fixtures.ts` is shared machinery, so this is a report item and not an edit. `forbidRelationships` does not share the defect — a non-null value routes to the `meta.` branch and compares there — which is why the negative assertion is written this way and the null row above is kept as the statement of intent rather than deleted.

The same invariant on the POSITIONAL spelling, which carries the same `meta.isComObject: null` (inert) row above. Two forbids rather than one because the mutant keys on the target's punctuation and flips every dotted target it sees, so a single forbid would be caught by whichever row happened to be checked first — two rows make the invariant a property of the construct (a non-COM construction never claims COM) rather than of one fixture line.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: Three spellings, three edges. A fix that read `-ComObject` but not the positional form scores 2 and fails; one that dropped the accelerator guard scores 4 and fails. The count is what makes the guard and the positional form independently load-bearing rather than one row carrying both.
